sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. (Isabi = language I1)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' in the volume; I1 forms carry no stress or tone marks, visual check printed p. 8). Intro sec. 3, p. vi: 'Isabi and Biyom languages are tonal and they are the only tonal languages so far known within the Adelbert Range language group.' Sec. 9 p. viii-ix: semi-phonemic transcription, Isabi segment fluctuations only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.8.2.2.2.6 'The Brahman Languages', p. 586: 'Isabi is heavily influenced by the East New Guinea Highlands Stock languages (Wurm, personal communication) and appears to be tonal.' Nothing on stress; classification and pronoun remarks only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
